get.summary:
The current rate to convert one unit of from into
to. 503 is this endpoint's distinctive failure: the provider's own
retry budget (ADR 0014) has already been exhausted by the time one reaches a caller here.

post.summary: Adds a product to the catalogue and returns its new identifier.

get.summary: Lists the catalogue newest first, one page at a time.
Fetches a single product by its identifier.

put.summary: Replaces a product's editable fields. The sku is not among them.

post.summary:
Asks for a PDF of every order the caller has placed. Built in the background; the caller is
notified when it is ready. While one is still being built, returns that one rather than
starting another.

get.summary: The caller's exports, newest first. Kept for seven days.

The PDF of a Ready export. 404 if it is someone else's or not built yet — the same answer for
both, so an export id reveals nothing. The viewer fetches this same URL for the bytes.

post.summary: Places an order and returns its new identifier.

get.summary: Lists orders newest first, one page at a time.

post.summary:
Cancels one of the caller's own orders. 409 if it has already shipped or was already
cancelled.

get.summary: Fetches a single order by its identifier.
Lists the caller's notifications, newest first, one page at a time.
The caller's unread count, for a badge.

post.summary:
Marks one notification read. Idempotent — marking an already-read one answers 200 with a
MarkedCount of zero, not an error.

get.summary: Confirms monitoring access and identifies the operator.
The dead-letter queue.

post.summary: Puts one dead-lettered message back in play.
post.description:
The API marks the stored envelope replayable and stops there; the worker picks it up from
the shared PostgreSQL store on its own. The two hosts never talk, which is what makes this
page possible without exposing the worker through the ingress. See ADR 0016.

get.summary: The job-run table, newest first.
One attempt, with its full error text.
Counts by outcome over a trailing window, for the overview tiles.

post.summary: Runs a scheduled job now, without waiting for its cron.

get.summary: Counts by outcome, the locked-out accounts, and the active-user count.
The sign-in audit trail, newest first.
Traffic over a trailing window, whole and per endpoint or handler.
The per-minute series behind the traffic chart.
The accounts, most recently seen first.

post.description:
Does NOT end the target's sessions, deliberately: the role is read from the database on
every request, so a demotion takes effect on their next one without signing them out of a
session they still hold legitimately. Use `sign-out` below for that.

post.summary: Revokes every session the account holds, by rotating its security stamp.

get.summary: What has been done to one account, newest first.
Every buyer's orders in one status, oldest first, one page at a time.

post.summary:
Marks any buyer's order as shipped. 409 if it has already shipped or was cancelled — an
illegal transition is a conflict with existing state, not a malformed request.
Creates an account and signs it in.
Signs in with a username and password.
Signs out, clearing the session cookie.
post.description:
Anonymous deliberately: signing out when the cookie has already expired is the caller
getting what they asked for, not an error worth a 401.

get.summary: Returns the signed-in user.

post.summary: Changes the signed-in user's own password.
Invalidates every session for the signed-in user, including this one.

AdminActionKind.description: What one administrator did to one account.

AdminActionResponse.description: What an administrator did to an account.

roleIsConfigured.description:
Whether this username is named in `Admin__Usernames`. Configuration is a floor
(ADR 0022): demoting an account that is still listed there is undone at the next API
start, so the screen warns before the click rather than after the restart.

lastSeenAt.description: Null for an account that has never made an authenticated request.

AdministeredUserResponse.description: One account on the user-management screen.

CancelOrderRequest.description:
The reason is owned by `CancelOrderValidator`, not duplicated here as a DataAnnotation —
see the note on PlaceOrderRequest.

ChangeUserRoleRequest.description: The role to move an account to.

CreateProductRequest.description:
Business-rule validation (non-empty, max length, price range and scale) is owned by
`CreateProductValidator` in the validation behavior — not duplicated here as
DataAnnotations. See `src/Api/CLAUDE.md`.

replayable.description: True once an operator has asked for it to be retried.

DeadLetterResponse.description: A message that exhausted its retries, from Wolverine's own dead-letter queue.

description.description: The worst check's description. Never a host, path, body or secret.

stale.description: The worker has not rewritten this row for three minutes: it is history, not health.

tokenOk.description: Null when the system uses no token.

ExternalSystemRowResponse.description: One external system. ExternalSystemState? ExternalSystemRowResponse.State is null until the worker has checked it once.

ExternalSystemsResponse.description: Every external system's last health and last hour of traffic.

buyerUsername.description: Null only if the buyer's account row is missing — see `FulfilmentQueueRow`.

productName.description:
The catalogue product as it was when the order was placed. Null on orders that predate the
catalogue link.

deadLettered.description:
The WHOLE dead-letter queue, not just the window: a message stuck for a week is exactly
the one worth seeing, and windowing it would hide the oldest failures behind the newest.

triggerableJobs.description: The scheduled jobs this operator may start on demand.

JobHealthResponse.description: Counts by outcome over a trailing window, for the overview tiles.

envelopeId.description: Wolverine's message id. Stable across every attempt at the same job.

oneOf.description: Null only for a job missing from the registration list.

error.description: The exception's type and message. The full stack is in the log store.

traceId.description: The W3C trace id, for the deep link into the log store.

JobRunStatus.description: What became of one attempt at one job.

rememberMe.description:
Whether the session cookie outlives the browser session. Maps to the auth cookie's
IsPersistent, which is the whole of what "remember me" means under cookie authentication.

role.description:
Always UserRole.Admin on a successful response — the policy admits nobody
else. Returned anyway so the page can render who it is showing, and so a future read-only
operator role has somewhere to appear without a contract change.

traceLinkTemplate.description:
The log store's URL for one trace, with `{traceId}` where the 32-hex id goes; null
when none is configured, in which case trace ids are shown as text. Carried here because
every monitoring page already asks this endpoint, and because it is admin-only: a member
never learns where the log store is.

MonitoringAccessResponse.description: Who is looking at the monitoring page.

NotificationKind.description:
What a notification is about. Persisted by name rather than by number (see the EF
configuration), so the numeric values here are free to be reordered — but the NAMES are a
stored contract: renaming one orphans every row already written under the old name.

markedCount.description:
How many this call actually changed. Zero is a success: re-reading something already read
is idempotent, not an error.

unreadCount.description: The badge count after the change, so the client needs no second round-trip.

NotificationReadResponse.description: What both mark-read endpoints answer with.

kind.description:
Serialized as its NAME, not its number — `Program.cs` configures a
`JsonStringEnumConverter`, and the generated OpenAPI document and
`frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts` both carry it as a string union. A client switching on
this gets a compile error when a kind is added, rather than an unhandled integer.

subjectId.description:
The order or product this is about, for deep-linking. Null when the subject is gone or was
never recorded — see `Notification.SubjectId`.

readAt.description: Null while unread. The single source of read-ness; there is no separate flag.

status.description:
Serialized as its name. Failed is never stored: an export still Requested after 45 minutes
reads as Failed, because its build job has given up (ADR 0029).

rowCount.description: How many orders the file holds. Null until Ready.

OrderExportState.description:
An export as the caller sees it. OrderExportState.Failed is never stored: it is a
Requested export past TimeSpan OrderExport.StaleAfter, read at the time of asking.

productId.description:
The catalogue product as it was when the order was placed. Null on orders that predate the
catalogue link — those render as the bare sku with no price.

shippedAt.description: Null unless OrderStatus OrderResponse.Status is Shipped.

cancelledAt.description: Null unless OrderStatus OrderResponse.Status is Cancelled.

productId.description:
The catalogue product as it was when the order was placed. Null on orders that predate the
catalogue link — those render as the bare sku with no price.

OrderStatus.description:
Where an order is in its life. Persisted by name, like
NotificationKind — the names are a stored contract.

OrderStatus.Placed is first so that it is also the CLR default: rows written before this
column existed materialize as Placed, which is what they were.

OrderStatusResponse.description: What both transition endpoints answer with, so a client can render the new state.

PlaceOrderRequest.description:
Business-rule validation (non-empty, max length, positive quantity) is owned by
`PlaceOrderValidator` in the validation behavior — not duplicated here as
DataAnnotations. See `src/Api/CLAUDE.md`.

RegisterRequest.description:
Business-rule validation (length, charset, password policy) is owned by the validators in
`src/Application/Users`, not duplicated here as DataAnnotations. See `src/Api/CLAUDE.md`.

role.description:
What the caller may do beyond their own data. Published so the SPA can decide whether to
render the monitoring nav entry — cosmetics, not the control. Authorization is the policy
on the server, which reads the role from the database on every request and never from
anything the client was told. Crosses the wire as a NAME ("Admin"), via the
JsonStringEnumConverter registered on both JsonOptions types in Program.cs. See ADR 0020.

SessionResponse.description: Who the caller is. Carries no password material, by construction.

userId.description: Null when the attempt named an account that does not exist.

usernameAttempted.description: What was typed. The only record of an attempt against a name that does not exist.

outcome.description:
The distinction the sign-in endpoint itself never reveals: it answers every failure
identically, because a differing answer is an account-enumeration oracle (ADR 0006). An
operator investigating an attack needs the difference; an attacker must not have it.

activeUsers.description:
Users seen within the active window. A cookie session has no logout event to key off, so
"online" can only ever mean "seen recently" — the window says how recently.

SignInHealthResponse.description: Sign-in counts, who is locked out, and who is about.

SignInOutcome.description: What happened on one attempt to authenticate.

TrafficKind.description: What kind of work a traffic measurement counted.

TrafficPointResponse.description: One minute of the whole application's traffic.

name.description: A route template for HTTP, a request type's name otherwise. Never a raw path.

p50Ms.description:
Interpolated from summed histogram buckets, not derived from the mean — a mean cannot give
a percentile, and averaging per-pod means would be wrong even if it could. Null when the
window holds no measurements.

TrafficRowResponse.description: One endpoint's or handler's traffic over a window.

errorRate.description: Failed plus faulted, over total. Zero when nothing was measured.

UnreadCountResponse.description: The badge count, on its own so a client polling it transfers one number.

UpdateProductRequest.description:
No Sku: it is the catalogue's business key and the domain refuses to change it. No Id
either — that comes from the route, so a body that disagreed with the URL could not arise.

UserRole.description: What a user may do beyond their own data.
